% amsmath's \displaybreak, \allowdisplaybreaks, and \hidewidth in math,
% which MathJax lacks. \displaybreak and \allowdisplaybreaks only allow a
% page break, and \hidewidth only lets a cell stick out, so none of them
% shows on the page. \displaybreak before \\ in align, with its optional
% argument from [0] to [4], on a numbered row with a \label, after the row
% end in gather*, in multline, alignat, flalign*, and eqnarray, in a
% theorem, and in align*, with an \eqref to rows that have it. Then
% \allowdisplaybreaks and \allowdisplaybreaks[2] inside a display, and
% \allowdisplaybreaks[1] in the preamble. Then \hidewidth at the start of
% a matrix cell, at the end of an array cell, in pmatrix, bmatrix, and
% cases, in smallmatrix in inline math and in a footnote, and on both
% sides of a cell of a text tabular, which tex4ht sets outside MathJax.
% Then \displaybreak on rows with \notag and \tag, with no space before
% it or \\, with a space before [3] and \\[2pt] after, in a macro of the
% document, and on the last row; in numbered gather and flalign;
% \hidewidth in an align cell before \text, in aligned, and in a macro of
% the document; before \text in an align cell narrower than its column,
% and in a group in a matrix cell. \allowdisplaybreaks[1] in the preamble
% is only built. A cell narrower than its column goes to the side away
% from \hidewidth, as in the PDF. Last, mathtools's \coloneqq and
% \mathclap, whose MathJax extension must stay configured beside \hidewidth.
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsmath,amsthm,mathtools}
\usepackage{hyperref}
\allowdisplaybreaks[1]
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}
\newcommand{\brk}{\displaybreak[1]}
\newcommand{\hw}[1]{\hidewidth #1\hidewidth}
\begin{document}

c &= d
\end{align}
\begin{align}
e &= f \label{eq:two} \displaybreak[3] \\
g &= h \displaybreak[0] \\
i &= j \displaybreak[1] \\
k &= l \displaybreak[2] \\
m &= n \displaybreak[4] \\
o &= p
\end{align}
See \eqref{eq:two} and \ref{eq:two}.

x + y \\ \displaybreak[0]
z
\end{gather*}

= t

u &= v &\quad w &= y \displaybreak[2] \\

\end{alignat}
\begin{flalign*}

G &= H
\end{flalign*}
\begin{eqnarray}

\end{eqnarray}

\begin{align}

\end{align}
\end{theorem}
\begin{align*}
Q &= R \displaybreak \\
S &= T
\end{align*}
Rows \eqref{eq:arr} and \eqref{eq:thm}.
\begin{align}
\allowdisplaybreaks

W &= X
\end{align}
\begin{align*}
\allowdisplaybreaks[2]

\alpha &= \beta
\end{align*}
\begin{align}
a &= b \notag \displaybreak \\
c &= d \label{eq:n} \\
e &= f \tag{A} \displaybreak[1] \\
g &= h\displaybreak\\
i &= j \displaybreak [3] \\[2pt]
k &= l \brk \\
o &= p \displaybreak
\end{align}
Row \eqref{eq:n}.
\begin{gather}
x \displaybreak \\
y
\end{gather}
\begin{flalign}
x &= y \displaybreak \\
z &= w
\end{flalign}
